ProblemDetails.description: An error response in the Problem Details format (RFC 9457).

code.description: The stable error code, when the problem has one.

detail.description: What went wrong with this request.

details.description: Structured facts about the refusal, such as the entity or the path it concerns. Only some refusals have it.

errors.description: The fields or filters that failed validation. Only a validation or filter error has it.

requestId.description: The ID of the request, when the problem has one.

title.description: A short summary, usually the text of the HTTP status.

type.description: The problem type. It is `about:blank`: the status and `code` identify the problem.

author.description: The subject of the caller who posted or began it.

blocks.description: The structured parts a client renders beside the body, as posted or last edited; none once deleted.

items.description: Any valid JSON value: object, array, primitive, or null

body.description: The text, Markdown: the draft so far while composing; empty once deleted.

createdAt.description: When it was posted, or for a message begin started, when it began, in epoch milliseconds: its place in the conversation's order, which never changes.

editedAt.description: When it was last edited, in epoch milliseconds; absent when it never was, or once deleted.

edits.description: How many times it was edited; listEdits reads the text before each. 0 once deleted.

for.description: The subject the message was written for: the person the agent or service that posted or began it acted for (D77); absent when it acted for nobody.

id.description: The message's number on the instance: 1, 2, 3, ...; never reused.

lastReplyAt.description: On a top-level message: the greatest postedAt of its thread's posted or interrupted replies; absent while it has none.

mentions.description: The subjects the message names for someone to hear of it; none once deleted.

participants.description: On a top-level message: the subjects that have a posted or interrupted message in its thread, the top-level one included, the one whose latest such message is latest first, at most 10.

postedAt.description: When it came to stand, posted or interrupted, in epoch milliseconds: a post's time, which is its createdAt, or the time of the finish or the interrupt of a message begin started. Absent while composing, and on a message deleted while composing.

quotes.description: The id of the message of the thread the reply quotes.

reactions.description: The reactions, by emoji, in the order each emoji was first given: how many, and whether the caller is among them. None once deleted.

replies.description: On a top-level message: how many posted or interrupted replies its thread has.

resolved.description: On a top-level message whose thread is resolved: who resolved it, for whom when it acted for someone, and when.

stand.description: The message's place in the order the conversation's messages came to stand: 1, 2, 3, ... on the instance, given when it is posted, finished or interrupted and never changed. A streamed reply that began early and finished late stands after the messages posted meanwhile, so a reader compares it, not the id, with its read marker. Absent while composing, and on a message deleted while composing.

state.description: composing, posted, interrupted or deleted. A composing message holds its place while its author writes it; an interrupted one holds what its author wrote before it stopped appending; a deleted one keeps its place, its author and its replies, and holds no text.

thread.description: For a reply, the id of the top-level message whose thread it is in; absent on a top-level message.

via.description: The deployable of the service whose call posted or began it (D37).

count.description: Signed 64-bit integer; range bounded by JavaScript's safe-integer ceiling.

mine.description: Whether the caller reacted with the emoji.

post.description: Replaces a posted or interrupted message's body, blocks or mentions, keeping what it held before for listEdits; an edit by its author posts an interrupted message. Its author may, within the config's editWindowMs of its postedAt when it sets one; a caller holding moderatePermission may edit any message, at any time. A ref block not on the message before must name an instance the caller may read, and an attachment not on it before must be one the config's attachments allow; a code block equal to the one at its place before keeps its moves. Acting for the author is not being it: only the author's own subject, or moderatePermission, may edit.
